title: Playing at Love: Ambiguous Intimacy in Indian Emerging Adulthood
abstract: Romantic exploration is a central developmental task of emerging adulthood, yet its meanings in India are shaped by family expectations, city context, gendered safety, and digital dating cultures. This mixed-methods study examined intimate associations among 120 college-going emerging adults aged 18 to 25 years from New Delhi/NCT and Vadodara, supported by focus group discussions ( n = 20) and in-depth interviews ( n = 20). Findings showed wide recognition of friends-with-benefits (91.67%) and situationships (89.17%), while situationships were the most lived label (35%). Men endorsed stronger agapic love than women, and Vadodara participants endorsed stronger pragmatic and agapic love than New Delhi/NCT participants. Communion in sexuality correlated with all love styles, suggesting that emotional connection remained central across varied approaches to love. Qualitative accounts show that intimacy is about comfort, vulnerability, safety, privacy, physical involvement, and ghar (feeling at home). The paper conceptualizes Indian emerging adults’ romantic lives as structured exploration and argues for relationship education in higher education.
